about: Mutants of compiler/check/store, the self-hosted checker's tables (capstone S3a). Each is killed by a law of the package, run by TestCompilerStoreLawsRun through ergo test.

mutants.name: objref-kind-shift-short
mutants.rule: An ObjRef keeps the kind in its top 4 bits and the id in the low 28; a short shift mixes the kind with the id, so View reads another kind's table.

mutants.name: pool-row-unsorted
mutants.from: let sorted = slices.SortFunc(ts, func(a dense.ID[TKey], b dense.ID[TKey]) int { dense.Index(a) - dense.Index(b) })
mutants.to: let sorted = slices.SortFunc(ts, func(a dense.ID[TKey], b dense.ID[TKey]) int { 0 })
mutants.rule: A row is a sorted set of type ids, so two rows of the same types are one id whatever order a pass lists them in.

mutants.name: pool-row-keeps-repeats
mutants.rule: A row holds each type once: a row with a repeat is the row without it.

mutants.name: instance-list-drops-origin
mutants.rule: Instances of two origins at equal arguments are two types: the origin is part of the interned key.

mutants.name: open-bit-misses-param
mutants.rule: The open bit says whether a type mentions a type parameter; Subst trusts it to return a closed type at once.

mutants.name: subst-skips-row-resort
mutants.rule: Substitution into a row gives a sorted set again: the substituted ids are re-sorted and repeats dropped.

mutants.name: canon-drops-origin
mutants.rule: The canonical key of an instance names its origin by package path and name, so instances of two origins never share a key.

mutants.name: canon-row-in-local-order
mutants.rule: A row's canonical key lists its elements in key order, not in local id order, which differs in each package's pool.

mutants.name: canon-named-drops-path
mutants.rule: The canonical key of a named type names its package, so a.T0 and b.T0 are two types.

mutants.name: view-context-reads-laws
mutants.rule: View reads the table of the ref's own kind.

mutants.name: declare-leaves-scope
mutants.rule: Declare binds the name in the package scope, so Lookup finds the declaration.
